item.title: [New] Microsoft Sentinel blog lists the new data connectors announced at Ignite 2026
item.description:
New connectors can close log-source gaps without custom ingestion; each one is a decision about cost, table and analytics coverage.

Sentinel · Read the list, mark connectors for sources you ingest today through custom or legacy paths, and plan a migration test in a non-production workspace. Confirm in your own tenant.

item.title: [New] The Copilot desktop app's built-in browser on Windows and Mac gets enterprise policies for security, privacy, authentication, network and download control
item.description:
An in-app browser is a second browser on the endpoint; once BrowsingEnabled is turned on it must carry the same site, download and authentication restrictions as the corporate browser or it becomes a gap in web and data-loss controls.

Copilot · Keep BrowsingEnabled off unless there is a business need; if you enable it, mirror your Edge security, download and site-access policies in the new Copilot in-app browsing policies and test sign-in flows with a pilot group. Confirm in your own tenant.

item.title: [New] Purview Insider Risk Management adds alert classification (True positive, Benign, False positive), separate from alert status, from December 2026
item.description:
Classification becomes its own field, so IRM triage reports, tuning reviews and any process that reads alert status for outcomes need to read the classification instead.

Purview · Brief insider-risk analysts on the new classification step before December and update triage runbooks and reports that infer outcome from alert status. Confirm in your own tenant.

item.title: [New] Windows 11 shows where to tap a security key on display-based NFC readers; admins can switch the indicator through a new CredentialProviders policy
item.description:
Makes phishing-resistant security-key sign-in easier on tablets and convertibles, which removes one reason users fall back to passwords on shared or kiosk-style Windows devices.

Windows · If you roll out FIDO2 security keys on Windows 11 devices with display NFC readers, decide whether to enable the indicator with the CredentialProviders CSP or GPO and add it to your passwordless pilot. Confirm in your own tenant.

item.title: [Due in 4 days] Defender for Identity retires two classic alerts at the end of November: Remote code execution attempt and Suspected identity theft (pass-the-hash)
item.description:
Two identity-attack detections disappear from the SOC queue; any analytics rule, playbook or SLA keyed on their alert titles goes silent, and pass-the-hash on hosts without MDE is no longer alerted at all.

MDI · deadline 2026-11-30 · Before 30 November create the Advanced Hunting custom detection from Microsoft's RemoteCodeExecution query, confirm MDE covers every DC and tier-0 host for pass-the-hash, and repoint Sentinel rules and playbooks that match the two classic alert names.

item.title: [Due in 5 days] Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 drops Exchange.ManageV2 and Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 on 1 December; apps must move to Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage / .ManageAsApp and get fresh admin consent
item.description:
Every automation and third-party tool that administers Exchange through the Admin API needs a new consent grant this month; a rushed tenant-wide consent on an app-only Exchange administration permission is exactly the grant an attacker hopes to slip through, and a missed one breaks the tool on 1 December.

Exchange Online · deadline 2026-12-01 · Inventory service principals holding Exchange.ManageV2 or Exchange.ManageAsAppV2, grant the replacement only to apps you still need, verify their Exchange RBAC role, test, then remove the old permission before 1 December; alert on consent to Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp in AuditLogs.

Defender XDR · deadline 2026-12-02 · When the banner appears, review every imported role and scope under Permissions > Roles in the Defender portal, test an analyst and a Security Reader account against email, device and Sentinel views, move any role automation to the Defender RBAC Graph API, and update runbooks before 2 December 2026.

item.title: [New] Custom detection rules map up to four identifiers per entity and the same entity type more than once (preview from 17 November 2026)
item.description:
Richer entity mapping is what correlation, automatic attack disruption and the new alert grouping key on; a rule that maps only one weak identifier groups and correlates badly.

Defender XDR · Review the custom detections that drive automated actions and add the stronger identifiers (object ID, SID, device ID) to their entities before turning on alert grouping.

item.title: [New] Custom detection rules can group their own alerts into one incident by time frame and matching entities (preview from 17 November 2026)
item.description:
Grouping changes how many incidents a noisy rule opens and how the queue reads; a rule set to 'group all alerts into one incident' can fold an unrelated second intrusion into an incident an analyst already triaged, and a closed incident is never reopened, so a matching alert lands in a new one.

Defender XDR · Leave grouping off on high-severity rules until tested; for noisy rules, choose 'all entities match' rather than 'group all', and document the time frame so the SOC knows why an incident holds many alerts.
